operation_rules.trigger_condition: feature_type IN (pocket, slot, boss, contour) AND material IN (aluminium_6061, aluminium_6063, aluminium_6082, aluminium) AND machine_has_dynamic_milling_cycle = true

operation_sequence.notes: Adaptive/trochoidal roughing — constant chip load, high Vc, high fz. Replaces standard pocket_mill RF for aluminium when CAM supports adaptive clearing (Fusion 360 Adaptive, HSMWorks Adaptive, Mastercam Dynamic).
Standard finish pass after dynamic RF to achieve final dimension.

decision_logic.use_dynamic_mill_when: CAM system supports adaptive clearing AND feature depth > 3× tool diameter (high material volume)
decision_logic.fall_back_to_standard_pocket_mill_when: shallow features (depth <= 1.5× tool diameter) OR CAM system lacks adaptive cycle

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Milling — High-Efficiency Milling (HEM) strategies
source.secondary: Sandvik Coromant 'High-efficiency milling in aluminium', Application Guide 2023
source.motor_mount_validation: Observed in ALL 4 setup sheets as primary RF strategy: MOTOR_MOUNT_1 op1 S=4461 F=1491, MOTOR_MOUNT_2 op1 S=4065 F=1523. Toolpath names explicitly say 'DYNAMIC'.
source.notes: This is the dominant RF strategy used on the real motor mount. Standard pocket_mill at full radial engagement is the fallback. Implement as a feature flag in process_selection.py.

open_issues: Requires CAM system to support adaptive/trochoidal cycle — not universally available.
Dynamic milling for boss/contour (outer profile) is also used but at different engagement.

operation_rules.trigger_condition: hole_tolerance <= H7 AND hole_diameter BETWEEN 3 AND 20 AND is_standard_reamer_size = true

operation_sequence.notes: Centre drill to prevent drill wander. Standard — same as any other hole.
Drill to reaming allowance: nominal minus 0.1–0.3mm for diameters under 10mm, nominal minus 0.2–0.5mm for 10–20mm. Machinery's Handbook: 0.1–0.3mm undersize for HSS reamers in aluminium.
Reaming to H7 tolerance. Use flood coolant. Do not reverse spindle in bore — retract with spindle running.

cutting_parameters.coolant: flood (essential for aluminium — prevents built-up edge on reamer)

tool_specification.geometry: straight flute for through holes, right-hand spiral for blind holes
tool_specification.tolerance: h6 reamer for H7 hole — reamer is 0.01mm undersized from nominal

decision_logic.prefer_reaming_over_boring_when: hole_diameter < 20mm AND tolerance H7 or coarser AND standard reamer size available
decision_logic.prefer_boring_over_reaming_when: hole_diameter >= 20mm OR tolerance H6 or tighter OR non-standard diameter

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Reaming — Speeds and Feeds for Reaming, Allowances for Reaming
source.motor_mount_validation: NOT observed on Motor Mount (no reamed holes identified). Rule is Machinery's Handbook only.
source.notes: Motor Mount holes appear to be drilled to nominal — either tolerance is loose or the drawn tolerance was H9/H10. Reaming rule needed for any H7 shaft fit or dowel pin hole.

open_issues: trigger_condition requires tolerance field in feature JSON — not yet extracted by classify_features.py
Hole diameter classification for 'standard reamer size' needs lookup table

operation_sequence.notes: 7075 is harder than 6061 — keep same reaming allowance.

tool_specification.tool_type: carbide chucking reamer preferred over HSS for 7075
tool_specification.geometry: straight flute for through, right-hand spiral for blind

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Reaming; Sandvik Coromant aluminium grades guide
source.motor_mount_validation: NOT observed on motor mount.
source.notes: 7075 is more abrasive than 6061 — carbide reamer preferred.

open_issues: Same dependency on tolerance field as PS-AL6061-REAM-001

operation_rules.trigger_condition: hole_diameter BETWEEN 13 AND 32 AND (require_precision_bore = true OR programmer_preference = circular_interp)

operation_sequence.notes: End mill follows circular path (helical entry recommended). Tool diameter = largest end mill that fits bore with 1mm clearance on each side. For D16.1 bore, use D10 EM (leaves 3.05mm radial clearance each side). Multiple Z passes may be needed.
Single finish pass to bore diameter. Climb mill only.

cutting_parameters.tool_diameter_rule: bore_diameter * 0.55 to 0.65 — gives adequate chip clearance while maintaining rigidity

decision_logic.prefer_circular_interp_over_drill_bore_w: diameter BETWEEN 13 AND 32 AND (high positional accuracy required OR no boring bar available for mid-range diameter)
decision_logic.prefer_drill_then_bore_when: diameter BETWEEN 13 AND 32 AND tolerance H7 or tighter (boring bar gives better roundness)

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Milling — Circular Interpolation for Holes
source.motor_mount_validation: CONFIRMED — Setup 4 op 1+2: D16.1 bore at -37mm depth machined with D10 EM using PROFILE BORE circular interpolation at S=2500 F=800. Toolpath names: '10 ENDMILL PROFILE BORE 16.1 RF' and '...FINISH'.
source.notes: Current pipeline uses circular_interp only for d > 32mm. This rule extends it to 13–32mm range where the programmer may prefer circular interp over pilot+core drill (better positional accuracy, no tool change for pilot drill).

open_issues: Overlap with existing pilot+core drill rule for 13–32mm. Need decision rule DR-005 to choose between them.
setup_4 bore is at -37mm depth — unusually deep for circular interp, requires long-reach EM.

operation_rules.trigger_condition: feature_type IN (planar_face, step, shoulder) AND top_corner_radius IS NOT NULL AND top_corner_radius BETWEEN 0.5 AND 3

operation_sequence.notes: Bull nose (corner radius) end mill to blend top edge radius. Single finish pass — no RF needed as material removal is minimal.

tool_specification.tool_type: bull nose end mill (corner radius end mill)
tool_specification.corner_radius_mm: match top_corner_radius specification (typical: R0.5, R1, R1.5, R2, R3)

decision_logic.use_bull_nose_when: feature has a specified top corner radius (drawing callout or design intent) AND flat end mill would leave sharp corner
decision_logic.do_not_use_when: radius is > 4mm (profile_3d_contour with ball nose is more appropriate)

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Milling Cutters — Corner Radius and Bull Nose End Mills
source.motor_mount_validation: CONFIRMED — T8 D8R1 bull nose used in BOTH Setup 1 (op 16, '8R1 ENDMILL_TOP R FINISH', S=4500 F=1500) AND Setup 2 (op 8, '8R1 ENDMILL', same params). Used specifically for top-of-step radius blending.
source.notes: Bull nose operation is not in process_selection.py at all. The current code has no tool type 'bull_nose' and tool_database.json has no bull_nose tools. Implementation requires: (1) add to tool_database, (2) add process rule here, (3) add feature field top_corner_radius to classify_features.py output.

top_corner_radius field not extracted by classify_features.py — requires STEP file reading enhancement.

operation_rules.trigger_condition: feature_type IN (pocket, slot, step, planar_face) AND floor_corner_radius IS NOT NULL AND floor_corner_radius BETWEEN 1 AND 5

operation_sequence.notes: Ball nose end mill to finish floor with radius. Follows flat end mill pocket_mill FINISH pass. Removes the witness mark left by flat tool on floor radius.

stepover_pct_of_dia.notes: Small stepover for fine floor surface finish

decision_logic.add_ball_nose_floor_when: step or pocket has specified floor radius AND a flat end mill was already used for main pocket operation
decision_logic.skip_when: floor_corner_radius is None or zero (sharp floor acceptable)

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Milling — Ball-End Milling
source.motor_mount_validation: CONFIRMED — T9 D5 ball nose used in Setup 1 (op 17, '5 BALLNOSE STEP BOTTOM FINISH', S=2500 F=200), Setup 2 (op 9), Setup 3 (op 3). All at identical S=2500 F=200 — very conservative feed for surface finish.
source.notes: Ball nose floor finish is used after every step pocket machining operation in the motor mount. This is the standard sign-off for any feature with a floor radius. fz=0.04 is very light — prioritizes surface finish over cycle time.

open_issues: floor_corner_radius not extracted by classify_features.py — same limitation as bull nose rule.
Ball nose tool type is in tool_database.json? Needs verification.
3mm ball nose (T12) used in setup 2 for tight radius areas — smaller tool for constrained floor geometry.

operation_rules.trigger_condition: feature_type = chamfer AND chamfer_angle = 45 AND chamfer_depth_mm > 0.5

operation_sequence.notes: First pass at very low speed to position and engage chamfer tool accurately. Vc ~28 m/min, F=80 mmpm. This is essentially a 'find the edge' pass. Depth equals full chamfer depth.
Fast profile pass at full chamfer speed. Vc ~140 m/min, F=700 mmpm. Full chamfer profile in one pass.

cutting_parameters.coolant: air blast (no coolant needed for chamfer in aluminium)

decision_logic.use_two_pass_when: chamfer_depth_mm > 0.5 AND part has been previously machined (tool needs to locate on existing edge)
decision_logic.single_pass_ok_when: chamfer_depth_mm <= 0.5 OR chamfer is on raw stock edge (easy to locate)

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Chamfering and Deburring
source.motor_mount_validation: CONFIRMED — Setup 1 ops 18–19: T10 chamfer mill at S=900 F=80 then S=4500 F=700. Setup 4 op 3: T10 chamfer at S=900 F=500. Pattern consistent across setups.
source.notes: The slow first pass (S=900) is unusual — not a standard Machinery's Handbook recommendation. This is the programmer's technique to ensure the chamfer tool engages correctly on a previously machined edge without chatter or tool deflection. HIGH confidence because observed twice.

open_issues: The 'TOUCH' pass concept has no analog in current pipeline — would require new pass_type.
Whether pass 1 is truly necessary or a programmer habit — needs shop validation.

operation_rules.trigger_condition: feature_type IN (pocket, slot) AND pocket_depth_mm / pocket_width_mm > 5 (high DDR for end mill)

operation_sequence.notes: Single RF pass only. No finish pass listed on motor mount for deep narrow pocket. Stock 0.15mm XY only.

cutting_parameters.ap_mm: full depth in steps if feature_depth > 3× tool_diameter
cutting_parameters.coolant: flood (essential for chip evacuation in deep narrow pocket)

tool_specification.diameter_selection: largest diameter that fits pocket width with 10% clearance per side
tool_specification.notes: Motor mount: D3 EM at -41.5mm = L/D ratio 13.8 — exceptional. Normally avoid L/D > 8.

decision_logic.trigger_DDR_for_EM: em_depth_mm / em_diameter_mm > 5 → reduce feed 30%; > 8 → reduce feed 50%; > 10 → flag for manual review
decision_logic.always_use_flood_coolant: chip packing in deep narrow pockets is a major failure mode

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Milling — Long-Reach and Extended Shank Milling
source.secondary: Sandvik Coromant 'Long overhang milling' application guide
source.motor_mount_validation: CONFIRMED — Setup 4 op 4: D3 EM at -41.5mm depth (L/D=13.8). S=2800 F=500. Named '3 ENDMILL LONG POCKET RF'.
source.notes: Extreme L/D ratio observed. Current pipeline has no L/D check for end mill operations — always emits full-depth pocket_mill. This rule adds a DDR check for end mills analogous to the drill DDR check.

open_issues: L/D check requires tool reach data in tool_database.json — currently not stored.
Process_selection.py cannot currently trigger a 'long-reach' tool selection.

operation_sequence.notes: 7075 is harder and more abrasive than 6061. Reduce Vc by ~15%. Keep fpr similar.

vc_m_per_min.notes: 15% lower than 6061 due to higher hardness and abrasiveness

cutting_parameters.coolant: flood (mandatory for 7075 — chip welding risk higher)

operation_rules.trigger_condition: feature_type IN (through_hole, blind_hole) AND material IN (stainless_steel, stainless_steel_316) AND hole_diameter BETWEEN 1 AND 13

operation_sequence.notes: Centre drill critical for SS — work hardening makes re-location nearly impossible after surface is touched.

operation_sequence.drill_cycle: peck for DDR > 2 (lower threshold than aluminium due to work hardening)
operation_sequence.notes: Carbide or cobalt HSS drill. Do not dwell in hole — SS work hardens rapidly at low or zero feed.

vc_m_per_min.notes: Carbide drill. Use 8–15 m/min for HSS.

feed_per_rev_mm.notes: Higher than aluminium proportionally — maintains chip break before work hardening

cutting_parameters.coolant: flood (mandatory — SS heat buildup is severe without coolant)

tool_specification.tool_type: carbide drill preferred; cobalt HSS acceptable for small diameters
tool_specification.geometry: 130–135° point angle, thin web, split point for SS

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Drilling — Austenitic Stainless Steel; Table of Drilling Speeds
source.secondary: Sandvik Coromant 'Drilling stainless steel' application guide
source.motor_mount_validation: NOT observed on motor mount (SS not used on this part).
source.notes: Work hardening is the primary hazard for SS304. Peck cycle DDR threshold is lower (2.0 vs 3.0 for aluminium) because chips pack more easily and work hardening accelerates failure.

open_issues: DDR thresholds for SS are tighter than aluminium — would need separate DDR constants per material in process_selection.py

operation_rules.trigger_condition: feature_type = tapped_hole AND material IN (stainless_steel, stainless_steel_316)

operation_sequence.notes: Drill to full tap drill diameter. For SS, use tap drill at 65–70% thread engagement (vs 75% for aluminium) to reduce tapping torque and risk of tap breakage.
operation_sequence.tap_drill_table_note: Use same ISO 68-1 sizes but consider stepping up one size for deep blind holes

operation_sequence.notes: Rigid tapping (G84). Use spiral-flute tap for blind holes to evacuate chips. Never reverse tap without coolant flowing. Feed rate = spindle_rpm × thread_pitch.

vc_m_per_min_tapping.notes: Very slow — SS tapping generates significant heat and torque

cutting_parameters.feed_per_rev_mm: equals thread pitch (rigid tapping — feed must be synchronized)
cutting_parameters.coolant: flood — mandatory for SS tapping; sulphurised cutting oil preferred over water-soluble

tool_specification.tool_type: spiral-flute tap for blind holes, straight flute for through holes
tool_specification.material: HSS-E (cobalt alloyed) or carbide for repeated use
tool_specification.coating: TiN or uncoated — avoid TiAlN which increases friction in SS

decision_logic.prefer_thread_mill_over_tap_when: thread_diameter > M8 OR blind_hole_depth < 1.5× diameter (no chip space) OR tolerance is 6H or tighter

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Tapping — Stainless Steel; §Thread Milling vs Tapping
source.motor_mount_validation: NOT observed on motor mount.
source.notes: Tap breakage in SS is the single most common threading failure. Rigid tapping is essential — floating tap holders allow tool to slip, causing broken taps. Spiral-flute tap critical for blind holes.

open_issues: Sulphurised cutting oil is not water-soluble — conflicts with flood coolant systems that use water-based coolant. Shop must switch fluid or use neat oil applicator.

operation_rules.trigger_condition: feature_type = planar_face AND material IN (stainless_steel, stainless_steel_316)

operation_sequence.notes: Roughing pass. Max ap = 0.5mm (already in FACE_MILL_MAX_AP table). Exit cut direction important — tool must exit completely before retracting to avoid built-up edge.
Finishing pass. One clean climb-milling pass. Do not reverse over finished surface.

vc_m_per_min_rf.notes: Carbide inserts (PVD coated). Positive rake geometry.

tool_specification.tool_type: indexable face mill, PVD TiAlN coated carbide inserts
tool_specification.geometry: positive rake, sharp edge for SS — avoid large nose radius which increases cutting forces

operation_rules.trigger_condition: feature_type = tapped_hole AND (thread_diameter > 10 OR hole_type = blind AND thread_depth_mm / thread_diameter < 1.5 OR material IN (stainless_steel, stainless_steel_316, titanium))

operation_sequence.notes: Drill to minor diameter of thread (same as tapping pilot hole). Thread mill cuts the thread form — no different pilot than tapping.

Single-tooth or multi-tooth thread mill follows helical path. Left out of hole from bottom for blind, conventional approach for through. One thread mill can cut any pitch — no tap change for special pitches.

cutting_parameters.feed_per_rev_mm: varies by thread mill geometry — typically 0.03–0.08 per tooth

tool_specification.note: Multi-form thread mills must match thread pitch exactly; single-tooth is universal

prefer_tap_over_thread_mill_when: thread_diameter <= M8 AND material is aluminium or mild steel
rigid tapping G84 is available and reliable

decision_rules.name: Tap vs Thread Mill Selection
decision_rules.decision: Given a tapped_hole feature, choose between tap_rh (G84 rigid tapping) and thread_mill.

use_tap_rh_when: thread_diameter <= M8 AND material IN (aluminium, mild_steel)
logic.priority: If any thread_mill condition is met, use thread_mill. Tap_rh only when all conditions are comfortably met.

decision_rules.name: Ream vs Bore Selection for Precision Holes
decision_rules.decision: Given a hole with tight tolerance, choose between reaming and boring.

use_reaming_when: standard reamer size available (standard metric reamer catalogue)
use_boring_when: tolerance H6 or tighter (boring gives better roundness)
non-standard diameter (custom boring bar can be adjusted; reamers come in fixed sizes)
blind hole requiring flat bottom (reamer has chamfered tip leaving a conical floor)
use_circular_interp_when: hole_diameter BETWEEN 13 AND 32 mm AND positional tolerance is primary concern
no boring bar or reamer available for that diameter range
logic.priority_order: reaming > boring > circular_interp for tolerance control; circular_interp > boring > reaming for positional accuracy

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Boring vs Reaming — Process Selection
source.motor_mount_validation: Motor mount uses profile bore (circular interp) for D16.1mm — confirms that circular_interp is used in 13–32mm range on this job.
source.notes: Ream for standard tolerance H7–H8, 3–20mm. Bore for non-standard or tight tolerance. Circular interp when positional accuracy is primary.

decision_rules.name: Peck Drilling Trigger (per material)
decision_rules.decision: Given a hole with known DDR, select the appropriate drill cycle. Current rules use same DDR thresholds for all materials.

mild_steel_en8.notes: Chip control is harder in steel — start pecking earlier

stainless_steel_304.peck_increment_mm: 0.5× drill_diameter (very small peck — work hardening risk)
stainless_steel_304.notes: Strictest thresholds — SS work hardens, chips weld to drill flutes

source.primary: Chang & Wysk 'Introduction to Automated Process Planning Systems' Ch. 5; Machinery's Handbook §Drilling
source.motor_mount_validation: CONFIRMED for aluminium: D2.5 at DDR=6.4 → deep peck with 1.5mm peck. D3.2 at DDR=4.375 → peck with 1.5mm peck. Both match peck thresholds exactly.
source.notes: Current code uses same DDR constants for all materials (standard≤3, peck 3–5, deep>5). This DR proposes tighter thresholds for steel and SS. Implementation: read material from context and apply different constants.

decision_rules.name: Finish Pass Trigger for Milling Operations
decision_rules.decision: When to add a dedicated FINISH pass vs. single-pass operation.

always_add_finish_pass: feature_type IN (pocket, slot, boss, contour) — always RF + FINISH (already in process_selection.py)
Any wall with surface roughness requirement Ra ≤ 3.2 µm
Any wall that is a datum face or mating surface
skip_finish_pass_single_op_ok: feature_type = chamfer — chamfer_mill in one profile pass is acceptable
feature_type = slot AND slot_depth <= 0.5× tool_diameter (very shallow slot, one pass is fine)
face_mill with depth within max_ap — single FINISH pass only (already in process_selection.py)
add_ball_nose_floor_finish_when: step or pocket has floor corner radius > 0.5mm
Always after the flat-bottom pocket_mill FINISH pass

stock_to_leave_guidance.motor_mount_observed: 0.25mm XY for 8mm pocket (D/depth=14/8=0.57), 0.1mm XY for 10mm EM step

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Milling — Allowances for Finishing
source.motor_mount_validation: CONFIRMED — all pockets use RF + FINISH pass pattern. Corner clearing pass used when corner radius < primary tool radius. Ball nose floor finish added for all step features.
source.notes: The stock to leave is higher (0.25mm) when using a smaller end mill relative to the feature. This is because deflection is higher with smaller tools.

decision_rules.name: Circular Interpolation vs Pilot+Core Drill for 13–32mm Bores
decision_rules.decision: For holes in the 13–32mm range, choose between pilot+core drill sequence and circular interpolation (profile bore).

use_circular_interp_when: positional_accuracy is primary concern (circular interp gives better positional accuracy than core drill)
bore has high depth-to-diameter ratio (> 2.0) making boring bar difficult
bore is part of a complex pocket that is already being milled (no need to change to drilling mode)
programmer has access to long-reach EM that fits the bore
use_pilot_core_drill_when: high production volume (drilling faster than circular interp for simple through holes)
tolerance is loose (H9 or coarser) — drilling is adequate
bore is standalone (not adjacent to milled features — no advantage to milling mode)
use_boring_bar_when: tolerance is H7 or tighter AND diameter > 20mm (boring gives best roundness)
non-standard diameter with no EM that provides correct engagement ratio

source.primary: Machinery's Handbook 29th ed. §Hole Making — Circular Interpolation vs Drilling
source.motor_mount_validation: CONFIRMED — Setup 4: D16.1 bore at -37mm machined with circular interpolation (profile bore) using D10 EM. This is in the 13–32mm range where current code uses pilot+core drill.
source.notes: This is the most important decision rule to implement — the motor mount confirms that circular interp is the preferred method for mid-range bores (13–32mm) in this shop. The current pipeline always uses pilot+core drill for this range, which contradicts observed practice.
